topSignals.title: Reverion emerges as a new German SOFC entrant explicitly targeting AI data centers — €150M ($175M) Series B, 250 MW factory, Ceres-licensed stacks via Doosan.
topSignals.text: Munich-based Reverion (container-based biogas/natural-gas/hydrogen SOFC power plants, reverse-operable as SOEC) closed a Series B led by Kembara with Allianz, KfW Capital, Aurum Impact and Carbon Equity, to scale manufacturing tenfold to 250 MW/year and add up to 800 jobs; it is now searching for a German factory site (Landsberg district actively bidding), with no location chosen yet as of Oct 1. The company claims 74.2% electrical efficiency in live customer operation and is explicitly pitching on-site, gas-infrastructure-connected SOFC power as the answer to multi-year hyperscaler grid-connection delays. Its stacks are supplied by Doosan Fuel Cell under a ~$78M/£60M order announced Sept 18, using Ceres Power-licensed SOFC technology — a direct link between a tracked priority-adjacent stack maker (Ceres) and a fast-moving new entrant. This appears not to have been in the monitor before; flagging now as a catch-up item given its materiality. Dealroom, Munich Startup, Doosan/Ceres order PDF, drweb.de factory search

lcoe.text: New: Reverion's claimed 74.2% electrical efficiency in live customer operation for its containerized SOFC/CHP system (described by the company as nearly double a conventional generator and a thermal-power-plant efficiency record). This is a vendor claim for a biogas/gas-fed container system, not an independently audited figure — useful as a directional benchmark for CHP-configured SOFC rather than a drop-in LCOE input. Dealroom
